newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS MOVE INTO FIRST PLACE BY BLANKING LIGHTNING.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS MOVE INTO FIRST PLACE BY BLANKING LIGHTNING.

text.p: Martin Brodeur struck again, making 26 saves for his third straight shutout as the surging New Jersey Devils moved into first place with a 3-0 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning.

Brodeur notched his league-leading ninth shutout of the season and Bobby Holik and John MacLean scored first-period goals in a win that gave the Devils 99 points, one more than Philadelphia in the Eastern Conference with five games left.
New Jersey, winners of four straight, are four points behind the Colorado Avalanche for the NHL's best record.
Daren Puppa finished with 23 saves for the Lightning, who are 12th in the East, four points behind Ottawa for the eighth and final playoff spot with five games left.

Brodeur set team records for consecutive shutouts and eclipsed his own Devils' mark for longest shutout streak. He has not allowed a goal in 183 minutes, 24 seconds since the Flyers' Mikael Renberg beat him in a 4-3 loss on March 25.

Brodeur, who lowered his league-leading goals-against average to 1.89, has held opponents to two goals or less in 10 of his last 12 outings and improved to 11-1-1 since February 22 and 16-2-7 since January 24.
"We started to play well right before the All-Star break," Brodeur said. "We came out of it and knew what we were going after and we never looked back."
The Lightning were playing their first game since centre John Cullen was diagnosed with lymphoma, a form of cancer.

In Anaheim, Teemu Selanne had a goal and two assists and Paul Kariya snapped a second-period tie with his 42nd goal as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim clinched their first-ever playoff berth by edging the red-hot Dallas Stars 3-2.
Mikhail Shtalenkov made 25 saves for the Ducks, who are unbeaten in their last five games (3-0-2) and extended their home unbeaten streak to 13 games (9-0-4).

Kariya's goal, which came with nine seconds left in the second period, extended his point-scoring streak to 10 games. The Ducks also moved past Phoenix and Edmonton into fourth place in the Western Conference playoff race.

Mike Lalor and Dave Reid scored for the Stars, who had their 11-game unbeaten streak broken. Arturs Irbe made 25 saves, but lost for the first time in 10 starts since taking over the number one job from the injured Andy Moog.

In Buffalo, Miroslav Satan recorded his first career hat trick and defenceman Darryl Shannon had his first two-goal game as the Buffalo Sabres snapped a season-high six-game winless streak with a 5-1 victory over the New York Rangers.

Brian Holzinger set up three goals for the Sabres, who had been 0-5-1 in their last six games. Buffalo moved 10 points ahead of second-place Pittsburgh in the Northeast and need one point to clinch their first division title since 1980-81.

"It's a big character builder for our team, especially the way we played the last couple of weeks," Buffalo's Mike Peca said. "Building towards the playoffs, these kinds of games you want to play in and win. We were pretty proud of our effort."
Dominik Hasek made 20 saves for the win. He's yielded just four goals in three games since returning from a rib injury.

In San Jose, Stephen Guolla scored 35 seconds into overtime and Tony Granato recorded his second hat trick of the season as the San Jose Sharks defeated the Colorado Avalanche 7-6 as the worst team in the Western Conference beat the best.

Guolla took a pass from Jeff Friesen in the high slot, skated toward the net and wristed a shot through goaltender Craig Billington's pads for his 13th goal of the season and first career game-winner.
San Jose, last in the West with 60 points, won for just the third time in 13 games. The Stanley Cup champion Avalanche lead the NHL with 103 points.

In Vancouver, Theoren Fleury's goal 8:02 into the second period lifted the Calgary Flames into a 3-3 tie with the Vancouver Canucks in a battle of Western Conference teams on the outside of the playoff picture.
